solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arrived shortly, turning up with son for college

indicators.note: shortly asks for the word to be cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: arrived means came

indicators.note: turning says the little word up is spun round to read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone arrives briefly, shows up with their son, and they head off to college together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims CAME to CAM; 'turning' flips UP to PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university or college, so the word stands for the institution by metonymy.

clue.text: Await developments in a leaf attachment

indicators.note: in places the waiting word inside the article plus the leaf

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
to pend is to remain undecided, awaiting developments

explanation.surface: Waiting to see how a leaf's attachment to its stem turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaf' suggests foliage, which suits 'attachment', but here it is a page of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something attached to a larger body, such as a limb or an add-on.

clue.text: School research task needs to stand out

definitions.meaning: a piece of research work set at school

explanation.surface: A school assignment that has to be impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil's extended piece of research is a project, and to project is to jut out or protrude.

clue.text: Mountain runner regularly visited Sikkim

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the place name, starting with its first

explanation.surface: A mountain athlete made frequent trips to the Himalayan state of Sikkim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete, but it is a ski that runs over snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is the long runner fixed to a boot for sliding over snow on mountain slopes.

clue.text: Brilliance of girl shown endlessly in competition

indicators.note: in places the shortened girl's name inside the word for a competition

parts.note: a race is a competition

indicators.note: endlessly says the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Diana is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl dazzles everyone in a contest, though not quite completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the girl's final letter before 'in' puts her inside the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance and brilliance are synonyms for intense, shining light or glowing beauty.

clue.text: Dance of millions in Cuba — right for clubs

indicators.note: right for clubs means the letter for right replaces the letter for clubs
in puts the abbreviation for millions inside the country's name

parts.note: taken as written
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A dance performed by millions in Cuba, suitable for nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: M inside CUBA gives CUMBA; then R replaces C (clubs, from card games).
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Afro-Cuban origin.

clue.text: Race to put on vital headgear

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
key means vital or crucial
a derby is a bowler hat

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a race by putting on essential headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: A donkey derby is a comic donkey race held at British fetes and seaside resorts; a derby is the American name for a bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey derby is a light-hearted race in which riders on donkeys compete.

clue.text: One further person yet to be named

definitions.meaning: ... is the placeholder name for an unnamed team member

explanation.surface: A further player still to be announced for the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: A. N. Other is a British convention on team sheets for a player not yet chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an additional one, and split as A. N. Other is the stock name for someone unnamed.

clue.text: Transparent sheet left over instrument

parts.note: a cel is a transparent celluloid sheet that animators draw on
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A clear plastic sheet left lying over a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks positional, but it is O, the cricket abbreviation for a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: Partial metaphor is misplaced in a maxim

indicators.note: Partial says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a half-finished figure of speech sits awkwardly in a proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'in a maxim' cannot stand in for a noun; the definition is 'maxim', with 'in a' joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorism is a short pithy saying expressing a general truth, the same thing as a maxim.

clue.text: Casually play with pasta

definitions.meaning: to improvise idly on an instrument, as jazz players do
a long thin strip of pasta

explanation.surface: Fiddling idly with your spaghetti at the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodling is informal for idle improvising on an instrument, and the same word names a strip of pasta.

clue.text: Trendy food shop has to supply food, mostly tasteless

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a deli, short for delicatessen, is a food shop

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to cater is to supply food

explanation.surface: A fashionable delicatessen has to provide meals, but most of it is in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CATER to CATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indelicate means lacking refinement or tact, so a remark lacking good taste is tasteless in that sense.

clue.text: Show a case for taking fast before one took food

indicators.note: before places the word for fast ahead of the rest

parts.note: instant means immediate or fast
I is the Roman numeral for one
ate means took food

explanation.surface: Arguing the case for skipping a meal, despite having eaten earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like going without food, which suits 'took food', but it means quick.
explanation.definitionFit: To instantiate is to represent something by a concrete instance, giving an example of it.

clue.text: Top cover for American district gangster

definitions.meaning: in US slang the ... is a neighbourhood

explanation.surface: A lid for an American neighbourhood's top gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a head covering, US slang for a neighbourhood, and a clipped form of hoodlum.

clue.text: Obese, eating seconds, and not running

indicators.note: eating says one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: obese means fat

explanation.surface: A fat man tucks into second helpings and stops jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not running' is about dyes: a colour that does not run is colourfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast dye stays put rather than bleeding in the wash, the sense of colours that are not running.

clue.text: What rail services need accompanying words and music?

definitions.meaning: trains need track that is in good condition
a film's recorded songs and score

explanation.surface: Asking what the railway needs, and wondering about songs as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A film's recorded music and dialogue is its soundtrack; a railway in good repair has sound track.

clue.text: Uniform used on Royal Navy vessel

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A uniform worn aboard a Royal Navy ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, such as one for ashes or for brewing tea.

clue.text: Caught rewritten line by me in play

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters of these words are written out again in another order

explanation.surface: An actor caught out a misquoted line of their own in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges LINE BY ME into YMBELINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbeline is a play by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Broken arrester in device holding something back

indicators.note: broken says the letters of the words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A faulty arrester inside a gadget meant to hold things back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges ARRESTER and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A restrainer is anything that restrains, such as a mechanism that checks or holds back motion.

clue.text: What stands up like this out of hot footwear?

indicators.note: out of says the abbreviation for hot is taken away

parts.note: thus means like this
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a sock is an item of footwear

explanation.surface: A riddle: what rises upright like this after slipping out of warm socks?
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes H from THUS, leaving TUS. 'like this' seems to belong to the definition, but it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a tuft of grass that sticks up from the ground.

clue.text: Cat and comb ultimately makes catacomb?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A wordplay riddle: cat plus comb's end gives a catacomb?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: a catacomb is one kind of burial chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground burial place, so it is an example of a grave or burial vault.

clue.text: Member in the House that is born in Chelsea, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the two small pieces inside the club's word

parts.note: Chelsea is a London football club, an example of a team
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An MP born in the London district of Chelsea sits in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member in the House' suggests an MP but is a structural member of a building; Chelsea is a London football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie beam is a horizontal timber joining the feet of rafters, a structural part of a house.

clue.text: Deep sea fish, black when small

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A dark fish from the deep sea, when it is only a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on two senses: a deep voice and a sea fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass is the lowest male singing voice, so deep, and also a common sea fish such as sea bass.

clue.text: Parting device for stamping coins in gold

indicators.note: in places the stamping device inside the symbol for gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is the stamp used to strike coins

explanation.surface: A coin die set in gold, as a farewell gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell, a word said on parting.

clue.text: Surveyor's instrument — they cart me about

indicators.note: about says the letters of the fodder are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests at being wheeled around by a group carrying them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tachymeter is a theodolite used by surveyors to measure distances quickly.

clue.text: Young archer finished in police department

indicators.note: in places the word for finished inside the police department

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
up can mean finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: A young bowman whose career ended at the police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid, the Roman god of love, is pictured as a winged boy with a bow and arrows.

clue.text: Am keeping notes about sensitive plant

indicators.note: about tells you the whole assembly is turned round to read backwards
keeping says the word am holds the notes inside it

parts.note: taken as written
so and mi are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone says they are holding notes about a delicate plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts SO and MI inside AM to make ASOMIM; 'about' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa pudica is literally called the sensitive plant because its leaves fold when touched.

clue.text: Very poor walkway state getting turned round

parts.note: a path is a walkway

indicators.note: getting turned round says the word for state is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to state or quote

explanation.surface: A dreadful footpath whose condition is spinning out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a noun meaning condition, but it is the verb, to declare or quote.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic is used informally to mean miserably inadequate or very poor in quality.

clue.text: Wicket perhaps overturned endlessly in game

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue says the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top
endlessly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a wicket is a small gate, an example of one

explanation.surface: A cricket wicket knocked over, ending play in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicket' suggests cricket but is a small gate; 'endlessly' trims GATE to GAT, which 'overturned' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tag is a children's chasing game, also called tig or it.

clue.text: Briefly immerse pot for small plant

parts.note: to duck someone is to dip them briefly under water
pot and weed are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Dunk a pot quickly to grow a little plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' looks like a plant pot but is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Duckweed is a tiny floating aquatic plant that covers ponds.

clue.text: Good, I am allowed a cocktail

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone happily reports they are permitted a mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimlet is a cocktail of gin or vodka with lime juice.
